key_insight: MatScope finds that strong calculations and physical explanations do not consistently translate into accurate material-state comparisons or quantitative experimental decisions.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-assisted materials laboratories need condition-specific reasoning and evidence updates that improve predictions without destabilizing previously accurate judgments.
method: M1: Test unaided reasoning with 200 tasks across ten research functions using aluminium and high-entropy alloys.
M2: Evaluate agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20: Assess initial forecasts and revisions of hidden responses as observations accumulate.
evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, the evaluation reports stronger performance on given-input calculations and many physical explanations than on fine-grained estimates, similar-state comparisons and quantitatively supported choices.
watch_item: Related literature and new observations can help, but condition or baseline mismatches may limit knowledge transfer and destabilize accurate predictions.
paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
